newsitem.title: UK: Major says UK expects to hit inflation target.
newsitem.headline: Major says UK expects to hit inflation target.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Thursday told parliament his government still expects to hit its target of getting inflation down to 2.5 percent or below.
Major was replying to a question from Labour leader Tony Blair about figures published earlier showing that the retail price index minus mortgages rose 3.3 percent in October.
He said the October figures were "artificially high" because of a steep fall in prices in October 1995.
"Over the months ahead that will correct itself and we expect to reach our target," Major said. He did not give a forecast for when the figure would come down to 2.5 percent.
Major also welcomed figures on Wednesday showing a 40,800 drop in unemployment in Britain in October.
He said joblessness was "falling here in a way that cannot be seen anywhere else in the continent of Europe".
"I don't think that is unrelated to the fact that we have avoided the burdens on business which so many of our partners have accepted and would have been accepted by Labour," Major said.
